#: What release.py says while it builds the archive - read by whoever builds a release.
release.noFolder: could not find %(name)s; name its folder with an argument, or get it from %(source)s
release.noPart: %(name)s has no %(part)s in %(folder)s - the add-on is not the one expected
release.notTheFolder: %(folder)s has no %(files)s in it - this is not %(name)s
release.optList: what would go into the archive, doing nothing
release.optNoVendor: no third-party code at all: the workbench alone
release.optOut: where to put it; build\ by default
release.optStageOnly: stage the folder and do not pack it
release.tpIntro: morphbench is under the GNU GPL 3 (LICENSE next to this file). The package also carries work by other people:
release.tpOwnBody:
The GPL gives a right to the sources of everything that lies here. The sources of the
workbench travel in this very archive: it is the same Python that runs.
release.usage:
Building the release: one self-contained archive of the workbench.

    python release.py                      build into build\ and pack
    python release.py --version 0.7.0      release number for the archive name and manifest.json
    python release.py --no-python          no embedded Python (one must already be installed)
    python release.py --pynifly <folder>   take the add-on from here instead of looking for it
    python release.py --stage-only         stage the release folder and do not pack it
    python release.py --list               what would go into the archive, doing nothing
